metadata.title: The integral form L^A_{0,1} is an A-algebra generated by matrix coefficients with the naturality and fusion defining relations

statement_spans.label: author prop environment, source label defL01A (statement, source lines 760-761)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 765-777)

standard_prerequisites: The integral base ring A = C[q, q^{-1}]; the integral form O_A of O_q: a Hopf A-subalgebra of O_q which is a free A-module and a full A-sublattice of O_q, with O_A tensor_A C(q) = O_q.
The product of O_q on matrix coefficients, _{(V tensor W)} phi = _V phi * _W phi (source product relation (4.4), label mmtilde-1).
Proposition 4.1 (label L01surq): O_q endowed with the product (4.4) is a right module C(q)-algebra over U_q tensor U_q^cop, denoted L_{0,1}.
The naturality relations (4.11) (label naturality) and the fusion relation (4.12) (label fusionrel) as defining relations of L_{0,1}.
The product relation (4.8) (label devprodq): the R-matrix expansion of a product of matrix coefficients of two type-1 modules X, Y through the star product.
Theorem 3.2 (label integteo), part (1): the integral statement on structure coefficients of the integral form.
Matrix coefficients _X phi^{e^i}_{e_j} of U_A^res-modules of type 1 with dual bases (e_i), (e^i); the category C_A of U_A^res-modules of type 1.
core_obligations: Proposition 4.10 of the source: the space O_A endowed with the product (4.4) is an A-algebra, denoted L^A_{0,1}; moreover L^A_{0,1} is the A-algebra generated by the matrix coefficients _X phi^{e^i}_{e_j}, for all objects X of the category C_A, with defining relations (4.11) and (4.12).
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (A-linearity of the product): for an A-basis {alpha_i} of O_A write the product through Proposition 4.1 as alpha_i alpha_j = sum_k m^k_{ij} alpha_k with m^k_{ij} in C(q) (in-span equation (4.16)); expand each alpha_i over A as a combination of matrix coefficients of U_A^res-modules of type 1 and multiply two such coefficients by the R-matrix expansion (4.8).

Step 2 (coefficients land in A): the star products in the expansion are again in O_A, hence A-linear combinations of the basis; by Theorem 3.2(1) the remaining coefficients belong to C[q^{1/D}, q^{-1/D}]; since C(q) and C[q^{1/D}, q^{-1/D}] intersect in C[q, q^{-1}] = A, one gets m^k_{ij} in A, proving the first claim; the arguments of Proposition 4.6 apply as well to L^A_{0,1}, which implies the generator-and-relations claim.
metadata.difficulty_reason: A-integrality bookkeeping: the basis-expansion argument must combine the R-matrix product expansion, the A-spanning of O_A by matrix coefficients of U_A^res-modules, and the coefficient-ring intersection of C(q) with C[q^{1/D}, q^{-1/D}] in the right order.

metadata.title: L_{0,n} as right module C(q)-algebra over (U_q x U_q-cop)^{odot n} and as U_q-module algebra (braided tensor product)

statement_spans.label: author prop environment, source label defiL0n (statement, source lines 987-992)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 993-1013)

standard_prerequisites: The twist construction of Section 4: F = (R')_{23}(R')_{24} is a twist of U_q tensor U_q^{cop}; twisting D_q by F gives the Hopf algebra A_q; the twisted product (source (4.4), label mmtilde-1), alpha beta = sum over (F) of (alpha . F_{(1)}) star (beta . F_{(2)}), makes O_q(q^{1/D}) a right A_q-module algebra denoted L_{0,1}(q^{1/D}); the restricted product on O_q is defined over C(q) (Proposition 4.1, label L01surq), and the rewrite (source (4.7), label mmmtilde) expresses it via the star product and R-matrix hits.

The iterated twist: Hopf algebras U_q^{odot n} (twist of U_q^{tensor n} by the product of the J_k), the associativity equality (source (6.2), label assodot), A_q^{odot n} = U_q^{odot 2n}, and the twist element F_2 (source (6.3), label formulaF): F_2 = (Delta tensor Delta)(R') = R'_{23} R'_{13} R'_{24} R'_{14}; F(l,k) = (Delta^{odot l} tensor Delta^{odot k})(R'); the bicharacter identities (6.1).

L_{0,n}(q^{1/D}) is the twist by F_n of L_{0,1}(q^{1/D})^{tensor n}; its product is given componentwise by (4.4) and between distinct components a < b by the exchange relation (source (6.5), label commutrel): (beta)^{(b)} (alpha)^{(a)} = sum over (F) of (alpha . F_{(2)})^{(a)} (beta . F_{(1)})^{(b)}; the embeddings i_a and the notation (alpha)^{(a)} = i_a(alpha).

The right action of U_q tensor U_q^{cop} on O_q and the devissage rewrite (source (4.8), label devprodq) used to expand products of matrix coefficients; the universal R-matrix R with (id tensor S)(R) = (id tensor ell) R^{-1} (id tensor ell^{-1}), ell the pivotal element; matrix entries of R^{+-1}_{V_lambda,V_mu} lie in q^{+-(lambda,mu)} C(q) (Theorem 3.2(2), label integteo, is the stronger integral statement); matrix entries of ell lie in the ring A.

The coproduct Delta of U_q yields a morphism of Hopf algebras into A_q (Proposition 4.2, label copHopf), and the U_q-module algebra structure on L_{0,1} is obtained by pulling back the U_q tensor U_q^{cop}-action via Delta (comment after Proposition 4.2).
Remark 6.1 (label twistbraided): when A = B is quasi-triangular with R-matrix R and F = R', the twisted tensor product construction gives the braided tensor product of A-module algebras.
The right coadjoint action coad^r of U_q on L_{0,1}; Sweedler notation for Delta(y) = sum over (y) of y_{(1)} tensor y_{(2)}.
core_obligations: Proposition 6.2 of the source: the subspace L_{0,1}^{tensor n} inside L_{0,n}(q^{1/D}), endowed with the product defined by (4.4) on each component and by the exchange relation (6.5) between distinct components, is a right module C(q)-algebra over (U_q tensor U_q^{cop})^{odot n} inside A_q^{odot n}; it is denoted L_{0,n}. Moreover L_{0,n} is a U_q-module algebra, namely the braided tensor product of n copies of the U_q-module algebra L_{0,1}, with U_q-action, still denoted coad^r, given by the formula (source (6.6), label actionprod): coad^r(y)(alpha^{(1)} tensor ... tensor alpha^{(n)}) = sum over (y) of coad^r(y_{(1)})(alpha^{(1)}) tensor ... tensor coad^r(y_{(n)})(alpha^{(n)}) for all y in U_q and alpha^{(1)} tensor ... tensor alpha^{(n)} in L_{0,n}.
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (reduction): the product on L_{0,1}^{tensor n} is defined over C(q) within each component (i_a is a morphism of algebras and the product of elements of i_a(L_{0,1}) is defined over C(q) by Proposition 4.1); it remains to check that the exchange relation (6.5) is defined over C(q).

Step 2 (R-matrix expansion, proceeding as in (4.7) and (4.8)): for matrix coefficients of V_lambda and V_mu placed in factors a < b, rewrite the exchange relation (6.5) through the four R-matrices R^1,...,R^4 making up F_2 of (6.3): first as a double action term, then converting the right hits into left hits with the antipode, then expanding matrix-entry-wise into the products pi_{V_lambda}(R^1_{(1)} R^2_{(1)}) pi_{V_lambda}(S(R^3_{(1)} R^4_{(1)})) pi_{V_mu}(R^2_{(2)} R^4_{(2)}) pi_{V_mu}(S(R^1_{(2)} R^3_{(2)})) times the coefficient pair, and finally using (id tensor S)(R) = (id tensor ell) R^{-1} (id tensor ell^{-1}) to rewrite the pi-factors with inverse R-matrices: pi_{V_lambda}(R^1_{(1) -1} R^2_{(1)}), pi_{V_lambda}(R^4_{(1) -1} R^3_{(1)}), pi_{V_mu}(R^2_{(2)} R^4_{(2) -1}), pi_{V_mu}(R^3_{(2)} ell R^1_{(2) -1} ell^{-1}).

Step 3 (coefficient field): the matrix entries of R^{+-1}_{V_lambda,V_mu} belong to q^{+-(lambda,mu)} C(q), so the q^{+(lambda,mu)} and q^{-(lambda,mu)} factors cancel in the last expression; the matrix entries of ell belong to A; hence all coefficients of the sum belong to C(q) and the exchange product is defined over C(q).

Step 4 (U_q-module algebra): consider on L_{0,1} the U_q-module algebra structure obtained by pulling back the U_q tensor U_q^{cop}-action via Delta; by Remark 6.1 the twist by R' gives the braided tensor product, so L_{0,n} = L_{0,1}^{odot n} is the braided tensor product of n copies of L_{0,1}; the restriction of the U_q-action to each factor being coad^r, the formula (6.6) follows from the properties of actions of module algebras.
metadata.difficulty_reason: A 20-line proof whose load-bearing part is the four-fold R-matrix coefficient expansion of Step 2 (delivered entry-by-entry in the span, including the antipode conversion and the pivotal-element rewrite), plus the cancellation argument of Step 3; Step 4 is structural and cites the delivered Remark 6.1 and module-algebra formalism.

metadata.title: PBW basis of L-tilde_{0,1}, j isomorphism, injectivity of Phi_1 and center C(q)[omega]

statement_spans.label: author prop environment, source label drinfeldinj (statement, source lines 833-834)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 835-861)

standard_prerequisites: L-tilde_{0,1}: the algebra generated by a-tilde, b-tilde, c-tilde, d-tilde satisfying the relations of Lemma 5.1 (label genrel01) together with ad - q^2 bc = 1; j: L-tilde_{0,1} -> L_{0,1}(sl(2)) the unique algebra morphism sending x-tilde to x for x in {a,b,c,d} (source lines 828-831).

The RSD map Phi_1: L_{0,1}(sl(2)) -> U_q(sl(2)), alpha -> (alpha tensor id)(RR'), with its values on the generators (source (5.3), label phigen): Phi_1(a) = K + q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 FE, Phi_1(b) = q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})F, Phi_1(c) = (q-q^{-1})K^{-1}E, Phi_1(d) = K^{-1}.
The central element Omega of U_q(sl(2)) (its image under Phi_1 is (5.4)); the center of U_q(sl(2)) is the polynomial algebra C(q)[Omega].
Verma modules M_x of U_q(sl(2)), x in C^x, with basis vectors v_n and action Ev_0 = 0, Kv_n = x q^{-2n} v_n, Fv_n = v_{n+1}.
omega = qa + q^{-1} d is central in L_{0,1}(sl(2)) (Lemma 5.1).
core_obligations: Proposition 5.2 of the source: the monomials (a-tilde)^alpha (b-tilde)^beta (c-tilde)^gamma and (d-tilde)^delta (b-tilde)^beta (c-tilde)^gamma, where alpha, beta, gamma, delta in N and alpha >= 1, form a basis of L-tilde_{0,1} over C(q); moreover j is an isomorphism, Phi_1 is injective, and the center of L_{0,1}(sl(2)) is the polynomial algebra C(q)[omega].
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (basis): the given monomials generate L-tilde_{0,1} by inspection of the relations of Lemma 5.1; for linear independence, apply Phi_1 composed with j to a general linear relation: the generator formulas (5.3) turn it into relation (5.5) in U_q(sl(2)); acting on the Verma highest weight vector v_0 kills all terms with gamma = gamma' > 0, and the remaining Laurent polynomial in x (using delta >= 1) forces A = B = 0 on the gamma = gamma' = 0 slice; acting on v_1, v_2, ... and iterating the same argument kills every coefficient, giving linear independence.

Step 2 (isomorphism, injectivity, center): injectivity of Phi_1 composed with j gives j injective, and j is surjective because the un-tilde monomials generate L_{0,1}(sl(2)); hence j is an isomorphism and Phi_1 is injective. For the center: Phi_1(z) commutes with Phi_1(L_{0,1}(sl(2))), hence with K, E, F, so it lies in the center C(q)[Omega] of U_q(sl(2)); writing Phi_1(z) = P(Omega) = P(Phi_1(omega)) = Phi_1(P(omega)), the injectivity of Phi_1 gives z = P(omega).

statement_spans.label: author prop environment, source label fusrel (statement, source lines 682-691)

standard_prerequisites: Finite-dimensional U_q(g)-modules V, W of the category C with chosen bases (e_i), dual bases (e^i), and matrix units E_i^j; the flip map sigma_{V,W}: V tensor W -> W tensor V.

Universal R-matrix in Sweedler components R = sum_(R) R_(1) tensor R_(2) = sum_(R) R_(1') tensor R_(2') with components in U_q(g), its copy R', the antipode S, and the evaluated R-matrices R_{V,W}, R'_{V,W} in End(V) tensor End(W).

Matrix coefficients _V phi^{e^i}_{e_j} of U_q(g) generating O_q, their star product _{(V tensor W)} phi^{e^i tensor e^k}_{e_j tensor e_l} = _V phi^{e^i}_{e_j} * _W phi^{e^k}_{e_l} defining the product of O_q, and the loop algebra L_{0,1} built on O_q as a U_q tensor U_q^cop module algebra over C(q).

The matrix element M^V = sum_{i,j} E_i^j tensor _V phi^{e^i}_{e_j} in End(V) tensor L_{0,1}, its embeddings M^V_1, M^W_2 in End(V) tensor End(W) tensor L_{0,1}, and M^{V tensor W} defined through the standard isomorphism End(V) tensor End(W) isomorphic to End(V tensor W) (notation paragraph of source lines 660-681).

The product relation (4.6) (label relprod2) and the naturality relations (4.11) (label naturality) of the same article, together a defining set of relations for L_{0,1}; the coregular right and left actions of U_q on O_q.

proof_roadmap: Step 1 (equivalence with the product relation): expand both sides of the fusion relation coefficientwise using the star product and the isomorphism V tensor V* -> End(V); the two coregular-action identities convert the coefficientwise identity into an instance of the product relation (4.6), and the identification of matrix coefficients in i, j, k, l shows equivalence, so fusion plus naturality is a defining set of relations for L_{0,1}.

statement_spans.label: author prop environment, source label imagephi (statement, source lines 869-871)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 872-902)

standard_prerequisites: L_{0,1}(sl(2)): the algebra generated by a, b, c, d with the defining relations of Lemma 5.1; omega = qa + q^{-1}d is central in it.

The RSD map Phi_1: L_{0,1}(sl(2)) -> U_q(sl(2)), alpha -> (alpha tensor id)(RR'), with generator values (source (5.3)): Phi_1(a) = K + q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 FE, Phi_1(b) = q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})F, Phi_1(c) = (q-q^{-1})K^{-1}E, Phi_1(d) = K^{-1}.

U_q^lf(sl(2)) is the locally finite part of U_q(sl(2)) under the right adjoint action ad^r; by the result of Joseph--Letzter recalled in Remark 4.5, tilde U_q^lf(sl(2)) = U_q^lf(sl(2)); the inclusion U_q^lf(sl(2)) subset U_q(sl(2)) is strict since K is not in U_q^lf.
Phi_1 is injective (Proposition 5.2); Omega = Phi_1(omega) is the central element of U_q(sl(2)), invariant under ad^r.

V_k denotes the k+1-dimensional simple U_q(sl(2))-module of type 1 (highest weight k); U_q(sl(2)) is an ad^r-module algebra; the comultiplication formula of F and the q-binomial identity hold; the Alekseev map is an equivariant morphism of module algebras (Theorem 6.6), whose arguments establish equivariance of analogous maps.
core_obligations: Proposition 5.4 of the source: the RSD map yields an isomorphism of U_q-module algebras Phi_1: L_{0,1}(sl(2)) -> U_q^lf(sl(2)).
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (equivariance and injectivity): that Phi_1 is an equivariant morphism follows from the same arguments as for the Alekseev map (Theorem 6.6); injectivity was shown in Proposition 5.2.

Step 2 (image inside U_q^lf): for every integer m >= 0 the ad^r-action formulas (5.6) hold, ad^r(K)((EK^{-1})^m) = q^{-2m}(EK^{-1})^m and ad^r(E)((EK^{-1})^m) = 0, together with the seven displayed relations for ad^r(F)(EK^{-1}), ad^r(F^2)(EK^{-1}), ad^r(F^3)(EK^{-1}), ad^r(E)(K^{-1}), ad^r(F)(K^{-1}), ad^r(E)(F), ad^r(F)(F); these imply EK^{-1}, K^{-1}, F belong to U_q^lf, and since Omega is invariant under ad^r the generator formulas (5.3) put Phi_1(a), Phi_1(b), Phi_1(c), Phi_1(d) in U_q^lf, hence Im(Phi_1) subset U_q^lf.

Step 3 (weight-graded induction): Phi_1(c) is a highest weight vector for ad^r generating a copy of V_3; by induction on m >= 1, ad^r(U_q(sl(2)))(Phi_1(c)^m) = V_{2m+1}; in view of (5.6) it suffices to prove ad^r(F^k)((EK^{-1})^m) != 0 for all k <= 2m and = 0 for k >= 2m+1; the induction step uses the formula of Delta(F), the q-binomial identity and the module-algebra property to reduce ad^r(F^k)((EK^{-1})^{m+1}) to a three-term sum, the k = 2m+2 case reduces to a single term with factor -(q+q^{-1})F which is nonzero by induction.

Step 4 (surjectivity): the multiplication map (direct sum over m >= 0 of V_{2m+1}) tensor C(q)[Omega] -> U_q^lf(sl(2)) is an isomorphism as in Section 3.11 of Joseph--Letzter; since Omega = Phi_1(omega) and V_{2m+1} is generated by Phi_1(c^{2m}), one deduces U_q^lf(sl(2)) subset Im(Phi_1).

The commutation relation (source (6.5), label commutrel): (beta)^{(b)}(alpha)^{(a)} = sum over (F) of (alpha . F_{(2)})^{(a)} (beta . F_{(1)})^{(b)}.

R-matrix calculus: R_{V,W} = sum over (R) of R_{(1)} tensor R_{(2)} = sum over (R) of R_{(1')} tensor R_{(2')}; the components R_{(1)}, R_{(1')}, R_{(2)}, R_{(2')} of the universal R-matrix in U_q; (S tensor S)(R) = R; the isomorphism V tensor V* -> End(V), v tensor f -> (w -> f(w)v); the coregular left/right actions on matrix coefficients; the flip sigma_{12,34} of tensorands; F = R'_{23} R'_{13} R'_{24} R'_{14} (source (6.3), label formulaF); m denotes the product map of L_{0,n}; Sweedler notation.
core_obligations: Proposition 6.3 of the source: for every a < b the matrices M^{(a)} satisfy the fusion equation (4.12), the naturality relations (4.11), and the exchange relation (6.7). Moreover, all these relations determine the product of L_{0,n}. Hence the algebra L_{0,n} can be viewed as the quotient of the algebra freely generated over C(q) by the matrix coefficients (phi_V)^{(a)}, for all objects V and every 1 <= a <= n, by the ideal generated by the relations (4.11), (4.12) and (6.7).
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (generation and reduction): the fusion and naturality relations follow from i_a being a morphism of algebras; the matrix coefficients (phi_V)^{(a)} generate the subalgebras L_{0,n}^{(a)} and hence L_{0,n}; conversely, by Proposition 4.6 the fusion and naturality relations determine the product of L_{0,n}^{(a)}; therefore it is enough to show that the exchange relations (6.7) and the commutation relation (6.5) are equivalent.

The Alekseev map Phi_n: L_{0,n} -> tilde U_q^{tensor n} is injective and equivariant (Theorem 6.6, label Alekseevmap).

The formula (source (6.12), label phicommut): (id tensor Phi_n)(M^{(1)} ... M^{(n)}) = (pi_V tensor Delta^{(n-1)})(RR'), whose matrix coefficients are the images under Phi_n of the matrix coefficients of the products M^{(1)} ... M^{(n)}.

Theorem 4.3 (label drinfeldmap): the RSD map Phi_1: L_{0,1} -> U_q, alpha -> (alpha tensor id)(RR'), with its description of the image (used with Phi_n's equivariance to place Phi_n(alpha) in the centralizer of Delta^{(n-1)}(tilde U_q^lf)).

Remark 4.5(1) (label remlf): the ad^r(U_q)-module tilde U_q^lf is generated by the elements l_{-lambda}, so that commuting with tilde U_q^lf is the same as commuting with tilde U_q; hence the centralizer of Delta^{(n-1)}(tilde U_q^lf) equals the centralizer of Delta^{(n-1)}(tilde U_q).

standard_prerequisites: The Alekseev map Phi_n: L_{0,n} -> tilde U_q^{tensor n} is an injective equivariant morphism of module algebras (Theorem 6.6, label Alekseevmap: 'yields an embedding of module algebras'), so its image consists of elements equivariant under the paired actions.

The action (source (6.9), label coadmat): coad^r(y)(M_{ij}^{(a)}) = sum over (y),k,l of pi_V(y_{(1)})_{ik} M_{kl}^{(a)} pi_V(S(y_{(2)}))_{lj}, the coadjoint action on the generator matrix M^{(a)} in End(V) tensor L_{0,n}; L_{0,n} is a U_q-module algebra under coad^r (Proposition 6.2).

The action (source (6.11), label adjointactiononn): ad_n^r(y)(x) = sum over (y) of Delta^{(n)}(S(y_{(1)})) x Delta^{(n)}(y_{(2)}), the adjoint-type action of U_q on tilde U_q^{tensor n}, where Delta^{(n)} is the iterated comultiplication; (ad^r)^{tensor n} denotes the n-fold tensor product of the adjoint action ad^r of U_q on tilde U_q.

(tilde U_q^{tensor n})^lf is the set of locally finite elements of tilde U_q^{tensor n} for ad_n^r; L_{0,n}^{U_q} and (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^{U_q} are the invariant subalgebras of the U_q-module algebras L_{0,n} and tilde U_q^{tensor n}.

Universal R-matrix calculus: R_{12} = R tensor 1 placement conventions, Sweedler sums over (R), (R^{-1}), (y); the identity R_{12}^{-1} R_{01} R'_{01} R_{12} = R_{02} R_{01} R'_{01} R_{02}^{-1}, a consequence of the Yang-Baxter equation.
Main theorem of [KLNY] (cited in the proof): the set of locally finite elements of tilde U_q^{tensor n} for the action (ad^r)^{tensor n} equals (tilde U_q^{lf})^{tensor n}.
The RSD map Phi_1: L_{0,1} -> tilde U_q^{lf} is an isomorphism of module algebras (Proposition 5.4), in particular surjective onto tilde U_q^{lf}; tilde U_q^{lf} = U_q^{lf}.
core_obligations: Proposition 6.7 of the source: the Alekseev map sends L_{0,n} isomorphically onto (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^lf, and its restriction to invariant elements affords an isomorphism Phi_n: L_{0,n}^{U_q} -> (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^{U_q}.
proof_roadmap: Step 1 (image inside the locally finite part): by (6.9) the action coad^r on L_{0,n} preserves the spaces of matrix coefficients of each object V; since coad^r gives L_{0,n} a module-algebra structure, coad^r is locally finite; the equivariance of Phi_n then implies Im(Phi_n) is contained in (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^lf; Phi_n is injective, so it remains to prove surjectivity onto (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^lf.

Step 2 (the two actions are intertwined, case n = 2): consider psi: tilde U_q^{tensor 2} -> tilde U_q^{tensor 2}, a tensor b -> R_{12}^{-1}(a tensor 1) R_{12}(1 tensor b); a four-step align computation with Sweedler sums over (y), (R), (R^{-1}) shows ad_2^r(y)(psi(a tensor b)) = psi((ad^r)^{tensor 2}(a tensor b)), using the R-y commutation moves y_{(k)} R = R y_{(j)}; so psi intertwines (ad^r)^{tensor 2} and ad_2^r.

Step 3 (surjectivity): psi is an isomorphism, descends to (tilde U_q^{lf})^{tensor 2} -> (tilde U_q^{tensor 2})^lf, and satisfies psi(a tensor b) = sum over (R) of ad^r(R_{(1)})(a) tensor R_{(2)} b; for z in (tilde U_q^{tensor 2})^lf, psi^{-1}(z) is locally finite for (ad^r)^{tensor 2}; by the main theorem of [KLNY] the locally finite elements of tilde U_q^{tensor n} for (ad^r)^{tensor n} equal (tilde U_q^{lf})^{tensor n}, so psi^{-1}(z) lies in tilde U_q^{lf} tensor tilde U_q^{lf}; by the surjectivity of Phi_1 onto tilde U_q^lf, z = psi composed with Phi_1^{tensor 2} applied to some t in L_{0,1}^{tensor 2}; by the Yang-Baxter identity R_{12}^{-1}R_{01}R'_{01}R_{12} = R_{02}R_{01}R'_{01}R_{02}^{-1} one gets z = Phi_2(t), identifying L_{0,2} with L_{0,1}^{tensor 2}; hence Phi_2 is a surjection onto (tilde U_q^{tensor 2})^lf, and the generalization to any n is straightforward.

Step 4 (invariants): by the previous theorem the equivariance of Phi_n gives the inclusion Phi_n(L_{0,n}^{U_q}) inside (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^{U_q}; the argument of Steps 2-3 applies in particular to ad_n^r-invariant elements z in (tilde U_q^{tensor n})^{U_q}; together with the injectivity of Phi_n this inclusion is an equality, proving the second claim.
